title: Live audio fallback and media boundaries
prompt:
For each independent case explain diagnosis, the smallest justified action, verification and limits. Give advice only.

1. A customer starts a music spectrum monitor with keyboard or touch. On some visits play rejects, a panel can disappear while play is pending, and users can change their reduced-motion preference mid-song. A Bookmark button needs optional audio feedback. Describe how the interface should behave.

2. A product section scrubs a silent clip from page progress. A teammate says video always uses less bandwidth and wants a soundtrack to follow scroll. Decide what to keep and how to compare delivery formats.

3. A prerecorded product lesson needs topic labels as the viewer seeks in either direction and adjusts playback rate. It already has user-selectable captions. Choose how to implement labels and when a video frame callback is appropriate.

checks.reason: The plan must explain the live frequency analysis path.
The runtime preference needs an explicit fallback.
Timed labels should follow the cue state on the media clock.

rubric: Separate explicit activation, asynchronous playback, audio output and frame work. Handle rejection and retry; a late resolution after stop or unmount cannot start a source or loop. Reduced motion preserves an understandable static state while the user controls audio.

Default to silent with opt-in audio cues, one per committed bookmark and no cue when muted or disposed. Keep visible and programmatic confirmation of the bookmark and an audio fallback or meaningful text.
Keep scroll scrubbing visually driven and silent; compare transferred bytes, decoded memory and seek latency at comparable quality. Include a native-control or static fallback.

Derive annotations from current metadata cues, with native captions independent. Verify initial playback, seeks including cue-free gaps, pause and rate changes. Reserve a video frame callback for actual frame alignment.
Provide observable checks and evidence limits. Do not claim browser execution.

If separate playback controls disable themselves, preserve visible keyboard focus during a pending start, move it when the focused control becomes unavailable, and keep the focused starting action available when playback is rejected.
acceptance: Correctly route all three cases and preserve user control and semantic fallbacks under playback, lifecycle and compatibility failures.
